model.reference: frozen sklearn float64 predict_proba cast to float32; independent NumPy float32 export check

measurement_scope: Local CPU-only experiment with one HTTP process and one ORT worker. No authentication or multi-tenant isolation; loopback/trusted inputs only.
Both modes replay identical scheduled arrivals and inputs. Actual dispatch/header/server arrival lag is retained; timing is not perfectly deterministic.
Successful-request latency excludes rejected/timed-out work. All outcome counts and all-terminal latency are shown alongside it; throughput counts successes only.
End-to-end latency runs from client task dispatch through complete response decoding. Reference checks are outside that timer but affect client scheduling; this is not raw model/kernel latency.
Paired RSS adds near-contemporaneous HTTP and worker process observations. Shared pages may be counted twice; this is not unique physical RAM or model-only memory.
RSS sampling requests 5 ms intervals and can miss short spikes. Per-process OS lifetime high-water observations are retained separately, never added as a simultaneous peak.
The generator/controller and fixtures are excluded from service RSS. Audit buffers and HTTP/IPC overhead are included. Finite audit retention is checked for eviction.
Warmups, imports and startup are excluded from traffic measurements. Processes are fresh per trial; caches, thermals and same-host load-generator contention are uncontrolled.
No universal batching speedup is assumed. Tiny models may gain little or lose latency through batching. Results are descriptive on one host.
